results.title: October 8 Gold Market Analysis and Trading Strategy
results.description: Gold experienced another wide-range move on Wednesday. Price first broke below 4110 and dropped to around 4065 before rebounding sharply toward 4126, reclaiming the 4110 level and forming a strong V-shaped recovery. In my view, the most important point is that although gold briefly broke below a key support level, sellers failed to maintain downside momentum. The strong recovery suggests that buying interest remains significant around the lower levels. On the daily chart, gold recovered from the 4065 low and remains within the recent consolidation range. The horizontal support and trendline support around the recent lows are still holding, while bearish signals from the technical indicators are gradually weakening. However, I do not consider this a confirmed bullish reversal yet. The broader structure remains relatively bearish, the Bollinger Bands are still pointing lower, and the short-term moving averages have not been decisively reclaimed. Therefore, I believe the market is more likely to remain in a wide consolidation range in the short term. This type of market is particularly difficult to predict. Conventional technical momentum analysis can become less reliable when price repeatedly sweeps both sides of the range. My Market View The previous low near 4065–4066 was close to the triangle trendline support, while the daily candle did not establish a decisive close below 4100. This suggests that the downside structure has not yet developed into another sustained bearish move. For today, I will focus on 4150 as the first short-term resistance and 4170 as the stronger resistance level. If gold rebounds into these areas but fails to break higher and shows clear signs of rejection, I will pay closer attention to short opportunities. At the same time, I do not want to ignore the possibility of another bullish rebound. In a wide-range consolidation market, I believe the best approach is to remain patient and stick to one clear strategy rather than constantly changing direction based on every short-term move. I do not want to become aggressively bearish simply because gold falls, or blindly bullish simply because it rebounds. My overall preference is to sell rallies near resistance while keeping an eye on buying opportunities near major support. Short-Term Trading Strategy My primary focus is on selling near the upper part of the range, with buying near strong support as a secondary strategy. Short Setup Gold rebounds into 4170–4180 and shows clear signs of rejection. Entry: 4170–4180 Stop Loss: 4200 Target 1: 4140 Target 2: 4120 Extended Target: 4100 If price breaks above 4200 with strong momentum, I would abandon this short setup and reassess the market structure. Long Setup Gold pulls back toward 4100–4110 and shows clear signs of stabilization. Entry: 4100–4110 Stop Loss: 4090 Target 1: 4150 Target 2: 4180 Extended Target: 4200 If 4100 is decisively broken, I would avoid trying to catch the bottom and wait for a new setup. Final View Overall, I believe gold is still in a wide consolidation phase following the recent sell-off. The strong rebound from 4065 shows that sellers currently lack sufficient momentum to extend the decline immediately. For now, my preferred strategy is to sell rallies near 4170–4185 while considering long opportunities around 4100–4110 if support holds. The key levels I am watching are 4100–4105 on the downside and 4170–4185 on the upside. I will wait for a confirmed breakout before changing my overall trading bias.
